quick.summary: Set up warning lights on your data so you can fix errors before anyone sees.
quick.takeaway: Write rules for what is normal, and let the system check them daily.

beats.line: A leader said website visits were negative. How did I miss that?
You assumed the new records would look like the old records.
Think of your car. You do not check the engine oil daily.
No. I wait for a warning light to flash.
Exactly. We can set up lights for your tables as well.
The manual calls these automated data quality assertions.
Can I just say a daily warning check?
You can. You write a rule for what is normal.
Like saying visits can never be below zero.
So if the rule breaks, it warns me before anyone sees.
Yes. You fix the pipeline before they notice.

quiz.question: What is the best way to catch an impossible number early?
options: Write a rule that checks the data every day.
Read the entire table manually every morning.
Wait for a business leader to notice.
Delete any row that looks slightly suspicious.
quiz.explanation: You can write rules describing what is normal, and let the computer check them automatically.

quiz.question: A warning check allows you to fix the pipeline before users see the broken numbers.
quiz.explanation: If the rule breaks during your morning run, you can fix the issue before the dashboard updates.
